title: Joseph of Arimathea (Mark 15:42–47)
hookLine: a council member boldly asks for the body and lays it in a tomb

lines: EVENING, THE DAY BEFORE THE SABBATH.
cards: When someone dies, somebody has to do the practical things. Call the family. Sign the forms.
Pick the clothes. It's an unglamorous kindness, and sometimes a brave one. It's evening on the day before the Sabbath.
Jesus is dead. The disciples are gone. The law in Deuteronomy says a hanged body must not stay up all night, but this body is in Roman hands.
Somebody has to ask for him. And the man who does is someone Mark has never mentioned before.

teach.h: A COUNCIL MEMBER, WAITING FOR THE KINGDOM.
teach.b: Mark introduces him in one breath, in the King James Bible: "Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus."
A counsellor: a member of the council, the same council that just condemned Jesus. Mark earlier said all of them condemned him; Luke adds that Joseph had not agreed with their decision.
Honorable, Mark calls him, and waiting for the kingdom of God, the kingdom Jesus announced in Mark's first chapter. Then the verb.

teach.h: HE DARED: HE WENT IN BOLDLY.
teach.b: He went in boldly: the Greek word means he dared. Walking into the Roman governor's house to ask for the body of a man just executed as king of the Jews could cost him his standing, maybe more. He goes anyway.
Pilate is surprised Jesus is already dead, calls the centurion to confirm it, and gives Joseph the body.

teach.h: LINEN, ROCK AND A ROLLED STONE.
teach.b: Joseph buys fine linen, takes him down, wraps him, lays him in a tomb cut out of the rock, and rolls a stone against the door. Two people are watching: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses.
They see where he is laid, and that detail matters for Sunday. The disciples, who knew him best, are nowhere. The one who shows up is an insider Mark hasn't mentioned before.

teach.h: AND CRAVED THE BODY OF JESUS.
teach.b: Several churches keep a feast day for him. Sometimes courage is loud. Sometimes it's a respectable man asking an awkward question, then doing the heavy lifting himself.

how: On Holy Saturday some churches keep a quiet day of waiting by the tomb; in Orthodox churches an embroidered cloth showing the burial is carried in procession, and Joseph of Arimathea is honored with a feast day in several churches.

o: the young man who fled naked from Gethsemane
the husband of Mary, a carpenter in Nazareth
the council member who asked Pilate for Jesus's body

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: Joseph of Arimathea was one of the twelve disciples
he was a respected member of the council.
two women saw where Jesus was buried
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses.
the Greek behind went in boldly means he dared

games.q: you're a respected council member. the man you secretly hoped in has just been executed as a rebel king. the Sabbath is coming. what do you do?
o: go to Pilate and ask for the body.
games.why: Joseph went in boldly to Pilate, craved the body, and buried Jesus himself in a rock tomb.

practice: Think of someone who has died, a grandparent, a friend, someone you barely knew, and ask what kindness you could still do for them: visiting their grave, calling the person they left behind, telling their story to someone who never met them.
Pick the one that feels a little awkward, the one that takes a bit of daring. If you pray, you can remember them before God.

wordCard.voice: Joseph, the council member who dared to ask Pilate for the body of Jesus, and laid him in a tomb cut in the rock.

orig.note: Greek: having dared. Mark 15:43, behind the King James "went in boldly".

carryVoice: Your line: he went in boldly. The Greek says he dared. That's day two hundred twenty-eight.
